source.version_note: Published 28 September 2026, Frontiers in Psychology 17:1885843. Empirical study of human-driver scenarios; the autonomous-vehicle application is prospective.

citation.title: Goodness behind a wheel: moral judgment in realistic traffic simulations featuring Agents, Deeds, and Consequences

reading.source_scope_note: Human third-person evaluations of human-driver traffic stories, presented as text, desktop video or group 360-degree projection. No autonomous-vehicle or language-model choices, real-world driving behavior or clinical diagnosis tested.
access_limits: All 16 extracted pages read, including exclusion footnote, Bayesian analyses, tables, within-framework contrasts, limitations and references. Page8 table/figure visually inspected.

External supplement with complete scenarios, raw data, SAS/R scripts and primary scale-validation works were not opened or reproduced. Main article's references to an Appendix do not include a full scenario appendix in this PDF.

study_1.recruitment: Nearly4000 scholars who submitted to a bioethics journal; self-selected respondents, not a verified universal ethicist population
study_1.design: 2 presentation modes x 2 agent-character x 2 deed x 2 consequence, between-person component assignment; two scenario observations per participant
study_1.outcome: Mean personal and perceived-social moral acceptability,1–10,pooled based on reported Pearson r>.88
study_1.framework_measure: Modified11-item PPIMT; CFA chi-square(44)=322.10,RMSEA.12; 437 assigned dominant standardized-score category,20 pluralists
study_1.bayesian_comparisons: No marginal deed BF01=12.57; no audiovisual consequence BF01=6.87, conditional on specified default priors/models

study_2.groups: 73per group, classes alternately assigned; common group presentation up to25students
study_2.stimuli: Five scenarios,six mixed-valence combinations each, excluding fully positive/negative corners; each person watches15vignettes
study_2.outcome: Personal and perceived-social ratings kept separate; reported ICC.35
study_2.framework_interaction: Personal F(10,688)=1.73,p.071; BF01=62.57 for no interaction; within-framework contrasts not significant moderation evidence

summary: No new independent behavior. Add a second fully read research source to character-based moral judgment and retain boundaries for halo, outcome bias and apparent survey satisficing. The results support strong character-cue effects in these stimuli, not automatic ethical correctness, a tested AV policy, or a universal advantage of immersive presentation.

findings.term: Character cues dominate these human traffic judgments
findings.definition: Human observers use positive or negative depictions of the driver when judging the moral acceptability of a traffic event, with stronger character contrasts than the selected rule or collision contrasts in these experiments.
findings.novelty_rationale: The existing entry was defined from an earlier design paper. This later empirical article contributes a second fully read source and an observed human judgment effect, without duplicating the ADC framework or claiming machine virtue.

findings.evidence_scope: Study1 analyzed457 journal-mailing-list respondents; character contrast2.39/10,d1.21 and larger for desktop video than text. Study2 analyzed146students viewing projected traffic clips; character contrast2.83social and3.27personal. Both concern moral judgment of human drivers; strong unrelated cruelty/care cues may amplify the effect.
findings.boundary: Observed character influence is not automatically a bias or a normatively correct policy. Character cues include intent, care and cruelty, rather than a clean measure of stable virtue. No real AV decisions, first-person driving, legal standard, rights allocation or model subjective character is tested.

findings.term: A salient character manipulation is not automatically a halo effect
findings.definition: Strongly valenced character information can change overall evaluation without demonstrating that an irrelevant positive trait improperly spills into an unrelated judgment.
findings.novelty_rationale: A discriminant boundary between general character-based evaluation and the existing positive halo construct; no separate halo ID or supporting-paper count.

evidence.quote: drivers with strongly positive or negative character cues

findings.evidence_scope: Authors acknowledge abusive/caring-parent and violent-animal-hater portrayals may dominate much subtler rule and collision manipulations. Relative effect sizes therefore depend on stimulus strength.
findings.boundary: Do not infer a general human preference for virtue ethics, an irrelevant-trait bias, or moral permission to rank a person's right to road safety by prior reputation. Matched manipulation strength and relevance checks are needed.

findings.term: Outcome relevance is not by itself outcome bias
findings.definition: Human observers assign different acceptability ratings to stories with and without a minor collision; the outcome can be relevant to their overall moral question without proving irrational hindsight.
findings.novelty_rationale: Clarifies that manipulating consequences in an overall-event judgment is not automatically a direct demonstration of the narrower decision-quality outcome bias.

findings.evidence_scope: Study1 text/video consequence differences vary, and Study2 finds positive differences. No controlled analysis establishes that predecision information, expected risk and causal responsibility are identical and should rationally be evaluated identically.
findings.boundary: Moral acceptability, decision quality based on available information, actual responsibility and feelings about outcomes are separate. Favoring fewer harms can be justified; no objective error or AI output failure is demonstrated.

findings.term: Low rating variance is a survey exclusion proxy, not diagnosed laziness
findings.definition: The researchers exclude respondents with low variability in ratings as possibly undifferentiated responders; a flat response pattern alone does not establish low effort or intentional failure to complete a task.
findings.novelty_rationale: Avoid treating the paper's use of satisficing as confirmation of the existing task-abandonment label. The operational proxy can also capture legitimate consistent judgments.

findings.evidence_scope: Study1 excludes96 respondents using low variance across only two scenario judgments; Study2 excludes26 using PPIMT or vignette response variance. Effort, strategy and intention are not independently measured.
findings.boundary: Selection using the outcome can remove real moral consistency or indifference to the manipulated factors and change estimated effects. Completing a survey with equal ratings is not necessarily satisficing, and survey satisficing is not synonymous with AI stopping a task prematurely.

methodological_limits: Study1 response flow796-208-96-35=457 reconciles, but more than42% of recruits are excluded. Their initial approximately20% response rate is not the analyzed response rate of about11% of the near4000 invitations.

Study1 removes96 low-variance respondents based on their moral-judgment outcomes, not an independent attention task. With only two scenario scores per person, equal or close legitimate judgments can trigger exclusion; outcome-based selection can distort main effects and interactions.

Study2 excludes low variance in either PPIMT or vignette judgments, unlike Study1's explicit vignette-only criterion. This can remove moral pluralists or genuinely consistent raters. The same exclusion logic is not applied identically across studies.

Study1 is called a quasi-experiment and says participants are randomly assigned to combinations, but exact presentation-mode allocation and missingness by condition are not fully documented. Do not infer every selection process was randomized.

Study2 assigns classes alternately to groups and presents common stimuli in sessions of up to25. Participant random intercepts do not handle possible class/session clustering, collective timing or group order effects.

Two scenario families in Study1 and five in Study2 limit stimulus generality. Analyses describe participant random effects, not a sampled-stimulus random structure or generalization over arbitrary traffic situations.

Character is manipulated with vivid cruelty/care scenes, while deeds and outcomes are comparatively mild. Larger coefficients can reflect unequal manipulation strength, not that character is intrinsically the most important moral dimension.
The scenarios all involve human drivers. Any proposed AV character proxy through speed, courtesy or braking is an application requiring a direct first-person/AV study, as the authors acknowledge.

Presentation modes differ not only in sensory richness but also emotional impact, information timing, interpretation and social setting. Study2 changes sample, within-person design, scenarios and presentation together; it does not isolate the causal effect of greater immersion.
Matching expected ADC predictions more closely does not validate ecological accuracy. No real-traffic criterion, behavioral validation or improved cultural comparability is measured.

Study1 pools personal and perceived-social ratings after Pearson r>.88. Correlation is not measurement equivalence, latent unidimensionality or agreement. Study2 uses an ICC and keeps them separate; these assessments are not directly interchangeable.
Study1's modified11-item PPIMT CFA shows poor fit,RMSEA.12,despite high omega values. Reliability does not repair factor validity or establish reliable virtue/deontology/consequence categories.

Assigning a dominant theory from standardized factor scores with a .3 lead is not a clinical classification or demonstrated adherence to a coherent philosophical doctrine. The report's description of that threshold as a moderate effect size is not a validation of classification accuracy.
Study2 refers to15 PPIMT prompts whereas Study1 uses11 modified items. Cross-study moral-preference comparisons need exact instrument and scoring alignment, not an assumption of identical scales.

Within-framework significant contrasts do not establish moderation across frameworks. The article appropriately distinguishes this in Study2: omnibus personal interaction p.071, with default-prior Bayes factor favoring no interaction.

Bayes factors quantify relative evidence conditional on priors, included terms and random-effect structure. BF01 values do not prove universal identical moral judgments, philosophical consensus or practical equivalence at a prespecified margin.

Study2 excludes the all-positive and all-negative combinations, leaving six of eight factorial cells. This constrains interactions and generalization; simple effects and group-specific means depend on the remaining combination structure.

Textual rule violation is rated more favorably than compliance in Study1, and within selected deontologist groups in Study2. Contextual justification, wording interpretation and coding explanations remain unresolved; do not label these participants hypocritical or irrational from that contrast.

Table1 places interaction values .09,.11,.05 under the same final column headed Cohen d, while the footnote defines partial eta-squared; the values correspond approximately to F/(F+df2). These should be identified as partial eta-squared rather than compared with main-effect d.

For overall Deed, Table1 gives difference.14,SE.11,F.97,p.325. Under the stated single contrast,(.14/.11)^2 is about1.62 rather than.97; point estimate,SE or test specification needs clarification. No guessed correction is inserted.

Study1 narrative calls effects generally small to moderate despite character d1.21 overall and1.88 audiovisual in Table1. Use the reported estimates and manipulation limits rather than the blanket effect-size description.

Adjusted mixed-model dfs and sensitivity calculations depend on repeated-measure assumptions. A generic small-effect power statement does not ensure power for every subgroup interaction, exclusion pattern or test family.
No preregistration is identified in the supplied PDF. Analyses labeled planned/prespecified are reported as such by the authors but were not independently verified against a dated protocol.

The main text retains REDACTED placeholders despite a named university/IRB in the ethics statement. It describes participant consent, while the final statement says legal guardians/next of kin; clarify boilerplate and participant ages rather than infer unauthorized research.

WEIRD volunteer/college samples, uncollected licensing status, driving frequency and rule knowledge limit generality. Expert convergence or undergraduate judgments are not sufficient to establish a morally correct AV policy.

Primary works, full supplementary scenarios and raw analysis files remain unread. The paper's declared nonuse of generative AI and publisher-generated alt text are provenance statements, not a cause inferred for any reporting error.

cross_paper_learning.finding: The earlier ADC paper proposes the framework and VR methodology. This later empirical paper gives direct evidence of character-cue effects but confirms that all scenarios still concern human drivers. Proposed AV use and real-world ethical validity remain separate.

Dong measures moral-emotion words after sacrificial AV/human scenarios; this low-stakes human-driver study measures acceptability. Neither a stronger character contrast nor a more immersive display demonstrates emotion, a machine feeling or general normative correctness.

Across both studies, presentation and decision type alter judgment patterns. Controlled within-study manipulation is stronger evidence than declaring photorealism or immersion necessary by comparing different samples and experiments.

deferred.reason: These are named trait-scale dimensions summarized in methods, not a distinct newly observed AI behavior. Null exploratory associations do not validate a machine diagnosis; individual traits need their own definitions, measures and primary sources.
A context-sensitive format effect is observed, but its mechanism and normative error criterion are not isolated. Retain evidence under character judgment rather than inventing a general defect name.
A within-task absence of moderation with scale-validity limits is not a new behavioral mechanism or comprehensive expert ethical consensus.

deferred.term: Survey satisficing as an alias for task abandonment
deferred.reason: Response variance is only a proxy. The narrower exclusion rule does not establish the existing early-stopping behavior; a conceptual primary source is needed to review the broad old alias.

source_corrections.correction: Values approximately.09,.11,.05 correspond to partial eta-squared via the footnote, although the shared column heading says Cohen d. Do not compare them as d.
Reported .14/.11 squared differs from F.97. Preserve the reported test and flag the inconsistency rather than inventing a corrected estimate.

limitations: No new ID is warranted solely to increase the behavior count. This file enriches evidence and measurement boundaries in the existing ontology; no AI defect, clinical diagnosis, normative link or annual series is invented.

subsequent_source_checks.finding: The earlier 2025 ADC traffic study is now fully read. It reports a failed Pet scenario followed by exploratory Intersection-only analysis. Preserve that limitation when describing the later study as a replication.
